themes.reason: This directly establishes the core diagnosis: evidence that lobster and crawfish stocks are overfished and not meeting MSY, which is the central problem the policy addresses.

themes.theme: Economic Value and Employment of the Shellfish Sector
themes.reason: Provides background context on the scale and value of the sector, explaining why overfishing matters economically, but the diagnosis of overfishing itself does not depend on this data.

themes.theme: Legal Obligations and Sustainability Targets (MSY, CFP, MSFD, UK BAP)
themes.reason: Sets out the legal/administrative framework and definitions (MSY, CFP, UK BAP) that contextualize the overfishing problem, but is background detail rather than the substance of the diagnosis.

themes.theme: Protection of Berried Lobsters and Crawfish
themes.reason: Describes the specific mechanism (berried females) through which overfishing harms future stock recruitment, directly supporting why current practices are unsustainable and central to the diagnosis of the problem.

themes.theme: Market Failure and Economic Rationale for Intervention
themes.reason: Explains the underlying economic cause of overfishing (common resource market failure) and why landing berried females imposes external costs, forming the causal explanation at the heart of the diagnosis.
